slides.title: DOSY: deconvolve each attenuation, then correlate them across frequencies
slides.text:
What DOSY is · two operations on N attenuations
DOSY: deconvolve each attenuation, then correlate them across frequencies
PFG
1 signal → S(b) → fit → one D
DOSY
N signals → N × f(D) → correlate → δ–D map, one row per molecule
1
Input, not DOSY yet: the PFG experiment repeated at every gradient gives N attenuations S(b), one per frequency.
2
Operation 1 · deconvolve each attenuation into a distribution f(D): an inverse Laplace transform, ill-posed by nature.
3
Operation 2 · correlate the N distributions across frequencies: signals that share D go to the same row; a row is a molecule, not a signal.
Resolving attenuations is only half of DOSY: without the correlation across frequencies there is no map and no molecules.
DOSY in practice · diffatonce.com
04

Animation on real TP194 data: a gradient series of spectra; at one frequency the attenuation is extracted and deconvolved into a diffusion distribution; the step labels read deconvolve, map and correlate; sweeping every frequency builds the DOSY map, where resin signals align near D 0.33 and small molecules near 1.9, followed by the same dataset in DiffAtOnce Prime.
slides.notes: DOSY starts here, and it is two distinct operations. Repeating the PFG at every gradient gives one attenuation per frequency: that is the input. First: deconvolve each attenuation into a distribution of D, an inverse Laplace transform with no unique answer. Second: correlate those distributions across frequencies, because every signal of one molecule shares the same D and lines up on one row. Resolving attenuations is only half of it: without the correlation there is no map and no molecules, and both operations are where a method can invent a result. [Let the clip finish: real TP194, last frame in Prime.]

slides.title: Every term in b is a calibration
slides.text:
01 · Measure · Why it is hard
Every term in b is a calibration
S/S₀ = exp(−bD) ,  b = γ² g² δ² (Δ − δ/3)
g · gradient strength
Calibrated on a standard at the actual temperature. Enters squared.
δ · gradient pulse
Set by P30 and the gradient shape; the shape changes the area factor.
Δ · diffusion time
Set by D20 and the pulse-program timing; the correction depends on the sequence.
P90 · RF pulse
Measured on this sample, tuning and power. A wrong flip angle costs signal.
T · temperature
Stable through the ramp; the reference D depends on it. Drift drives convection.
b values · the ramp
Chosen from a pilot. Too flat or too steep and D is not identifiable.

slides.title: Calibrate the 90° pulse on this sample
slides.text:
01 · Measure · Problem 1 of 6 · the RF pulse
Calibrate the 90° pulse on this sample
p1 → zg → efp
Keep phase, receiver gain and D1 fixed while P1 grows.
The first null after the maximum is 180°: P90 = P180 / 2.
Pitfall: taking the 360° null doubles P90.
P1 depends on sample, tuning and power: never copy it from another tube.

slides.title: The sequence and the gradient shape decide what b contains
slides.text:
01 · Measure · Problem 3 of 6 · what b means
The sequence and the gradient shape decide what b contains
1
The shape enters through σ (its area: 1 rectangle, 0.90 SMSQ10) and κ: E = exp(−Dγ²δ²σ²g²Δ′).
2
The sequence sets Δ′: Δ − δ/3 (PGSE, PGSTE), − τ/2 for bipolar pairs, Δ − 2δ/3 for the double STE; with SMSQ10, ×0.81 and 0.301 δ.
3
Double STE cancels flow: q(t) changes sign, so ∫q dt = 0 while ∫q² dt survives. Cost: 4× less signal.
Same decay, wrong equation: the rectangular PGSE formula on SMSQ10 bipolar data gives D 20 % too low.
Shape factors and Δ′ from Sinnaeve, Concepts Magn. Reson. A 40 (2012) 39–65; q(t) and b = ∫q² dt computed in the animation.
DOSY in practice · diffatonce.com
12

Animation: four gradient shapes with their sigma and kappa factors and the generalized Stejskal–Tanner equation; then PGSE, PGSTE, bipolar STE and double STE drawn as RF, gradient, coherence order, q(t) and q squared, with Delta prime for rectangular and SMSQ10 gradients.
slides.notes: b is not a number you copy from a manual. The gradient shape enters through its area factor sigma and through kappa, and the sequence decides Delta prime. The animation builds q of t for the four sequences we actually use and shades q squared, whose integral is b. And the double stimulated echo cancels flow because q changes sign, at the cost of four times less signal.

slides.title: P30 and D20 are a trade-off, not a recipe
slides.text:
01 · Measure · Problem 4 of 6 · P30 and D20
P30 and D20 are a trade-off, not a recipe
1
δ = 2·P30 enters b squared (×4 when P30 doubles); Δ = D20 enters linearly and costs relaxation.
2
Pilot low, medium and high gradients: decay clearly, keep the last points above the noise.
3
A long Δ also exposes the sample to convection, exchange and other motion.
4
The probe rules: coil and amplifier set a maximum lobe duration and duty cycle. Beyond them: coil heating (TE drift, convection), unsustained shape (b nominal ≠ b real), eddy currents (D16 too short: phase and lineshape distorted).
300 µs barely decays; 1.2 ms falls to 5 % with SNR 14; 2.7 ms × 200 ms: tail in the noise and beyond the probe.
Teaching model (workshop repository): D = 0.8×10⁻⁹ m² s⁻¹, Gmax 0.5 T/m hypothetical, T₁ 0.8 s, T₂ 60 ms, σ = 0.003 M₀. Probe limit drawn (2.5 ms) illustrative: read your probe and amplifier specification.
DOSY in practice · diffatonce.com
17

Animation: a map of P30 against D20 split into three zones, barely decays, useful window and tail in the noise, with a cursor moving from 300 microseconds to 1.2 milliseconds and then to 2.7 milliseconds with D20 200 milliseconds while the 23-point decay on the right changes and falls into the noise band.
slides.notes: Two knobs. Delta, twice P30, enters squared; D20 enters linearly and costs relaxation. At 300 microseconds it barely decays; at 1.2 milliseconds it falls to five percent above the noise; at 2.7 and 200, the tail is lost. And the probe rules: beyond its maximum duration the coil heats, the shape is not sustained and eddy currents distort the line: the nominal b stops being real.

01 · Measure · Problem 5 of 6 · convection · the models
KK2-50: four ramps, six models, six values of D
1
Dₐₚₚ at 3.622 ppm: 0.545 → 0.872 from d20 = 100 to 175 ms (+60 %), each fit R² ≥ 0.998; extrapolated to Δ = 0, D₀ ≈ 0.107.

02 · Process · Problem 3 of 5 · the method families
Four families of methods, four assumptions
Isolated signal
Mono-exponential · NNLS
Prefers the minimal model. Risk: unstable peaks without regularization.
Broad distribution
Tikhonov · MaxEnt · PALMA
Prefers smoothness or entropy. Risk: merges close components.
Few components
ITAMeD (L1) · VP · SCORE
Prefers sparsity or a fixed model order. Risk: the wrong order looks precise.
Overlapping signals
MF · TRAIn-MF · SILT
Prefers structure shared across frequencies. Risk: spurious factors.
FISTA, ADMM and SVD are numerical engines, not physical models. Compare solutions with the same b values, noise and preprocessing.

slides.title: D becomes a radius, and a radius becomes an apparent mass
slides.text:
02 · Process · Problem 5 of 5 · from D to size and mass
D becomes a radius, and a radius becomes an apparent mass
Rh = k_B T / (6 π η D)
η must be the viscosity of this solvent at this temperature; unknown η stays unknown, never zero
log₁₀(D η∞) = −0.568 log₁₀(M) − 1.775
PS high-dilution calibration; PPG: slope −0.546. Concentration model: D η_c = D η∞ · exp(k(M) C), C = m_solute / m_solvent
What it gives
D peak, D mean, mean Rh as the signal-weighted mean of Rh(D), apparent molecular moments and a signal-weighted dispersity.
What it does not
An absolute mass for star, brush or branched architectures; a molar fraction from a signal fraction; a validated uncertainty for a regularized width.
What the report keeps
Model family, equation, k, ν, C, weighed masses, viscosity, temperature, factors and warnings, with the source hashes.
DOSY in practice · diffatonce.com
36
slides.notes: The number everyone wants is a mass, and the road has three assumptions. Stokes-Einstein needs the viscosity of this solvent at this temperature. The molecular models are empirical calibrations, polystyrene and polypropylene glycol at high dilution. The result is an apparent mass, within the domain of the calibration, and the report keeps every ingredient.

03 · ResinAtOnce · convection
Convection: diagnose it, then measure a control
Diagnosis: six flow families are compared on the signed attenuation (diffusion only, Gaussian, two symmetric, uniform, two Gaussian, uniform ⊗ Gaussian). Insufficient evidence is reported as inconclusive, not as no convection.

Physical correction needs the sequence moments, the RF coherence pathway and the real gradient shapes, reviewed by a specialist. A scalar from the internal standard is not proof that convection is gone.

slides.title: stebpgp1s1d + SMSQ10.100
slides.text:
Appendix · the equation behind the TBO profile
stebpgp1s1d + SMSQ10.100
b = 0.81 (γ g δ)² [Δ − 0.32525 δ − τ/2]
δ = 2 × P30
P30 = 600 µs per lobe → δ = 1.20 ms. P1 is the RF pulse and never replaces P30.
τ = D16 + P2
Saved values: D16 = 1 ms, P2 = 31.6 µs → τ = 1.0316 ms. The TBO profile approximates τ ≈ D16 and declares it.
area = 0.90
In b: 0.90² = 0.81. It is the area factor of this shape, not a property of the probe.
0.32525
Theory for the bipolar smoothed square: (6344π² − 207)/(19440π²) ≈ 0.3252585656; the profile keeps 0.32525.
Shape, timings, G and Dref(T) must belong to the same experimental profile; the empirical b₁₀₀ belongs to the conditions where it was measured.
SI units: s, T/m and γ in rad s⁻¹ T⁻¹ give b in s m⁻². GPZ6/100 is a fraction of the calibrated maximum amplitude. Source: Sinnaeve, Concepts Magn. Reson. A 40 (2012), Table 2, p. 58.
DOSY in practice · diffatonce.com
63
slides.notes: Reference, not presented. This is the model the shared TBO profile uses for stebpgp1s1d with SMSQ10.100. 0.81 is 0.90 squared, the area factor of the shape. The theoretical timing coefficient is about 0.3252585656; the profile keeps 0.32525. P30 of 600 microseconds per lobe gives delta 1.20 ms. In this sequence tau includes d16 and p2; the profile approximates tau by D16, and that approximation is declared, not hidden. If Delta, delta or the shape change, recompute b with the matching model and check the standard.

CONTIN
Positive continuous distribution with regularization and its own parameter selection.
Fixed-lambda Tikhonov is not the full CONTIN program.
SVD / TSVD
Diagnose informative rank; compress the problem or truncate weak modes.
SVD alone does not guarantee positivity; more bins do not create resolution.
FISTA
Numerical engine for L1 or L2 objectives with projection/proximal operators.
The engine alone defines neither the prior nor the experiment.

Adaptive local smoothing for sharp peaks and broad regions.
